gates.reason: The server fixture isolates HOME and CLAUDE_DIR, clears authentication and LLM-egress settings, uses a fixture-only GitHub token, binds to loopback, and installs a fixed-host fetch-denial shim before server startup.
The restart detector test uses explicit snapshot provenance fields and verifies expired or disabled snapshots are omitted, not marked stale/revalidating, and do not reuse the prior ETag.
Process output is capped, fetches and startup have explicit timeouts, polling is bounded, and temporary resources are cleaned up.
The host-side CLI performs no network or shell execution; module imports are fixed under PROJECT_DIR, and user paths are passed as data to the graph builder rather than interpolated into commands.

The wrapper preserves typed anchor identity, rejects ambiguous or nonnumeric issue anchors, forwards ranking/status parameters, and emits only the structured injection produced by the provenance-aware neighborhood builder.
The host-side producer performs one graph build and one neighborhood calculation, supports max-distance and max-nodes limits, and emits a single JSON payload without repeated recomputation.

Child execution uses execFile with a fixed Node executable and fixed loader/producer paths, avoiding shell interpolation; fixtures are confined to a generated temporary directory and removed afterward.
The test reproduces ranking from an on-disk fixture and explicitly verifies demotion, dated asOf metadata, stale/contradictory flags, ambiguity sources, and structured observation provenance.
Child execution has a 30-second timeout and an 8 MiB output cap, and each small temporary fixture is removed in a finally block.
Image references are read as data and quoted in docker invocation and diagnostics; no eval or shell reconstruction is used, so refs cannot become additional command arguments.
The script does not produce recommendations, parse evidence, calculate metrics, or emit validated fix snippets.
Retries are bounded per reference, use explicit linear backoff, stop immediately on success, and preserve an aggregate failure status.
All filesystem reads target fixed repository paths or the exported docs-map relative path; the test performs no writes, network calls, shell execution, or secret handling.
The parity checks require the committed artifact to exist, remain within the parser byte cap, satisfy the strict parser contract, and retain consistent locator plumbing.
The test enforces the docs-map bounded-read byte budget and performs only a fixed number of synchronous reads during CI.
The PR identifier is restricted to digits and all GitHub CLI calls use execFileSync argument arrays rather than a shell; no repository secrets are printed by normal paths.
Milestone routing is workflow policy, not recommendation evidence, detector provenance, historical-signal reporting, arithmetic, or a validated fix snippet.
This is a one-shot CI administration command with a constant number of GitHub CLI calls, not hot-path or ingest/assemble code.
The unit test imports pure milestone-selection functions and performs no authentication, filesystem access, network access, command execution, or secret handling.
The assertions cover workflow milestone naming and ambiguity policy, not recommendation evidence, detector provenance, arithmetic, historical signals, or validated fix snippets.
The file is a small standalone unit test over fixed in-memory arrays and does not exercise a hot path or ship a runtime surface.
